title: Unified idempotency, hedging, and load-shed contract for multi-region failover
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Services and SDKs currently have inconsistent retry semantics across regions which causes duplicated side-effects, uneven failover behavior, and hard-to-diagnose latency spikes during partial regional outages. This ticket defines a unified contract (headers, SDK helpers, runtime signals, and defaults) for idempotent retries, hedged requests, and load-shedding to enable predictable multi-region failover and SLO alignment.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Runtime accepts standardized idempotency and hedge headers and logs canonical fields. 2) SDKs (python/js/go) expose helpers to create and attach idempotency keys and hedge hints. 3) Circuit breaker and load-shed triggers documented and wired to existing console alerts. 4) Canary enablement shows no increase in duplicate side-effects beyond 0.1% and preserves SLOs for p50/p95 latency. 5) Playbook for regional failover references these headers and shows a tested fallback sequence.
technical_considerations: - Backwards compatibility: server accepts both legacy X-Idempotency-Key and new X-Redwood-Idempotency-Key and normalizes to internal idempotency_id. - Client-side: SDKs must not enable hedging by default for non-idempotent endpoints. - Hashing: store only keyed hash (sha256) of idempotency key on the runtime side to avoid PII. - Observability: emit idempotency.cache_hit, hedge.attempts, shed.reason as metrics on token-level sampling. - Security: keys may be user-supplied; limit size and reject non-utf8; die on suspicious reuse patterns.
idempotency_spec: Header: X-Redwood-Idempotency-Key (string). Optional body field: idempotency_key for JSON POSTs. Requirements: client-generated UUIDv4 or server helper-generated UUID+timestamp. Server stores sha256(key||route) -> response fingerprint TTL 24 hours default (configurable per-route). Responses must include X-Idempotency-Status: stored|replayed|new. Duplicate detection dedupes side-effects for up to TTL. For long-running operations, clients may set X-Idempotency-TTL to extend (max 7 days).
hedging_spec: Header: X-Redwood-Hedge-Policy (json-ish string): {strategy, max_hedges, hedge_delay_ms}. Default strategy: conservative. Default hedge_delay_ms: 350ms. Default max_hedges: 1 (single extra concurrent attempt). Hedge requests inherit idempotency key. Hedge attempts must use region-aware routing: prefer local region first; hedged attempts may route to secondary region only after hedge_delay_ms. SDK will expose request.with_hedging({delay_ms, max_attempts}) and runtime will reject hedged requests for non-idempotent endpoints. Hedged responses are deduplicated by idempotency store and only the fastest valid response is returned to caller.
circuit_breaker_spec: Policy named: cb.dynamic_default. Inputs: rolling window 60s, min_calls 50, error_ratio_threshold 0.12, latency_threshold_ms p95 > 2000ms. State machine: CLOSED -> HALF_OPEN -> OPEN. Open duration 30s with exponential backoff up to 5 minutes on repeated triggers. While OPEN, requests receive 503 with X-Redwood-Failover-Reason: circuit_open. Half-open uses 10% sample traffic. Circuit events published to console trace and alert rule cb.high_error_rate.
load_shedding_signals: Signals used by runtime: queue_depth_per_worker, kv_cache_miss_rate, token_backlog_seconds, tail_latency_ratio (p99/p50 > 5x). Sheds prioritized by route weight: best-effort endpoints (low-cost) -> background tasks -> interactive generation. Shed response code 429 with body explaining suggested retry-after header. Runtime attaches X-Redwood-Shed-Reason and X-Redwood-Queue-Depth headers for debugging and retrospective analysis.
rollout_plan: 1) Spec PR to confluence + internal RFC (done). 2) Runtime change: header parsing and idempotency-store shim (canary on api-dedicated-1) (2 weeks). 3) SDK updates: python/js/go 1.2.0 with helpers (parallel). 4) Enable hedging off by default; enable per-route via console flag for canary customers. 5) Gradual ramp: 0% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 2 weeks with automated rollback on duplicate-side-effect > 0.1% or p95 latency regression > 10%. 6) Postmortem evaluation and doc updates.
risks: - Incorrect idempotency usage by customers could mask real duplicate work. Mitigation: SDK helpers and runtime warnings. - Storage cost for idempotency entries at high QPS. Mitigation: TTL tuning, adaptive sampling for extremely high-volume endpoints. - Hedging increases peak load if misconfigured; mitigate via per-tenant quotas and max_hedges globally. - Cross-region eventual consistency may produce replay windows; document expected behaviors.
test_plan: Unit tests for header parsing and normalization. Integration tests: simulate multi-region latency skew and verify hedging behavior and deduplication. Chaos tests: bring down primary region and assert failover route and circuit behavior. Load test: synthetic traffic to validate idempotency store sizing and expiry. SDK e2e tests generating idempotent requests with hedging enabled.
